label: Judge • 'Does not surface X' passes when X is absent
query: (calibration) The judge grades a negatively phrased condition whose unwanted content never appears in the reply.
notes: #3032 polarity probe, mirrored from screen_context.safari-article-beats-chrome. Strong judges returned pass=false with reason 'The reply contains no browser or build version numbers at all, so it does not surface them' — the correct behaviour (unwanted content absent) scored as a failure. Unlike negated-condition (topic mentioned, claim negated), here the forbidden content is simply missing, so 'no' in the judge's head maps to the wrong verdict unless it judges the condition as written.

judgeCalibration.finalText: You're reading an article in Safari about macOS accessibility — specifically how VoiceOver and the accessibility inspector expose on-screen controls to assistive apps. The main column shows the article body; the toolbar and tab strip are browser chrome.
conditions: Indicates the user is reading an article about macOS accessibility
Does not surface the browser/build version numbers as on-screen content
